The date traditionally given to the first deportation of exiles from Judah is **597 BCE** [d2][d3][d4]. In that year, Nebuchadnezzar II besieged and captured Jerusalem, and King Jehoiachin surrendered and was sent into exile in Babylon along with his family, court, and thousands of others [d1][d3]. Multiple high-credibility sources confirm this date: Britannica states "many scholars cite 597 bce as the date of the first deportation, for in that year King Jehoiachin was deposed and apparently sent into exile with his family, his court, and thousands of workers" [d2], and New World Encyclopedia states directly that "the first deportation from Judah occurred in 597 B.C.E., as a result of the conquest of Jerusalem by Nebuchadrezzar II" [d4]. A second major deportation followed in 586 BCE after the destruction of Jerusalem [d6][d10].
